items.title: Nvidia stock falls amid probe into CEO’s relationship with Chinese spy
items.summary:
By Steve Kopack and Rob Wile

Nvidia’s stock slid about 4% on Monday after the company announced that it had opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman that U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.

The probe has the potential to unsettle the entire AI boom, fueled by trillions of dollars of spending and investments, in part to purchase Nvidia’s cutting-edge AI chips. Nvidia’s drop wiped out more than $200 billion in value. [...] Nvidia’s peers, such as AMD, Qualcomm, Taiwan Semi and Intel, all rose along with the broader market. Nvidia was the biggest loser on the Dow, the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500.

With so many outstanding questions about the Huang scandal, few major analysts that cover Nvidia had weighed in on Monday morning about what it could mean for the company’s future.

But those who did said it was a blemish on an otherwise sterling track record, which could spark even more investigations. [...] “A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation,” Nvidia said in a Sunday statement. “The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”

An Nvidia spokesperson told NBC News that Huang was “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.”

items.title: Harness Engineering 2.0 is here!
items.summary:
Harness Engineering 2.0 is here!

After protocols for tools, agent communication, and agent interfaces, harnesses now have one too.

Developers just built UHP (Unified Harness Protocol), a standardized interface for running agent tasks across any agent harness.

HarnessRouter is its open-source server implementation.

Here’s how it works:

- The product backend sends a task with a `harness_id`.
- HarnessRouter starts the selected harness in its own session.
- The harness runs its native agent loop and streams back progress.
- Files, artifacts, failures, and the final output return through the same interface.

Without UHP, integrating every harness needs separate handling for task execution, sessions, streaming, files, recovery, and output formats.

With UHP, Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Hermes, Pi, and other harnesses can plug into the same product backend while keeping their native tools, skills, models, and agent loops.

This means developers can:

- Switch harnesses without rebuilding the product integration.
- Run the same task across different harnesses.
- Add new harnesses without maintaining another execution stack.

HarnessRouter currently supports 30 harness bases.

Here’s the repo: https://t.co/scJwb2xUyM

(don’t forget to star it ⭐)

As per official benchmarks, changing only the harness while keeping the model fixed reduced costs by 25% to 64% across several healthcare compliance tasks.

And changing both the harness and model widened the difference to 99.8% between the highest and lowest-cost configurations.

Developers can test their own workloads across different configurations using Harness Arena.

Alibaba Cloud's Qoder has also adopted UHP, making it available as an agent backend through the HarnessRouter API.

If you want to dive deeper, I already wrote an article that explains why model routing is different from harness routing and what supporting multiple agent runtimes actually involves.

It also covers UHP, the local setup, a working API call, and how sessions and files work.

Read it below.

items.title: do you understand what just happened to your computer..
items.summary:
do you understand what just happened to your computer..

Google Chrome secretly downloaded a 4GB AI model onto your device. Without asking.. Without telling you..

It's called weights.bin. It lives deep in your system folders. It powers Gemini Nano - Google's on-device AI.

And if you delete it? Chrome re-downloads it automatically. Like nothing happened.

Just Google deciding your hard drive is their storage unit.

At 1 billion Chrome users - that's 4 BILLION gigabytes of data pushed silently across the internet. 

The carbon footprint alone equals tens of thousands of cars running for a year.

Check your disk right now:
📁 %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\OptGuideOnDeviceModel

To stop it: chrome://flags → disable Optimization Guide On Device Model → restart Chrome → delete the folder.

Reshare so people know what's sitting on their computers.

results.facts: - The Telegram bot can send messages only after explicit confirmation. - If the user says "đăng", "gửi", or "post" without confirming the exact text, ask for yes/no confirmation first. - Keep a transcript showing the confirmation before sending.
